subject: DeeplyHealth: tenant access corridor & API key plan
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@deeplyhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@deeplyhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: DeeplyHealth: tenant access corridor & API key plan

Hi Chloe / Monica,

Thanks for the quick discovery session earlier — looping in Mark (infra) so he has visibility. We want to get the initial tenant spun up and API access seeded this week so our engineering team can start smoke testing. High-level asks: 

- Two environments: staging (for immediate integration tests) and prod (locked down).
- Admin roster for both envs (3 people for prod, 2 for staging) — I attached a short requirements list.
- SSO: we will provide SAML metadata (will attach in next email).
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault for key escrow and need guidance on how Redwood recommends connecting customer-managed KMS (prefer a step-by-step).
- Key rotation cadence: want a recommended schedule and whether Redwood supports automated rotation for API keys or only manual.

Could you propose a minimal handoff plan with owners and dates? Also let us know what artifacts you need from security (SOC2 report / questionnaire). Ideal timeline: staging ready by 11/02 and prod by 11/06, but flexible if you advise otherwise.

Attachments: initial_requirements.docx

Emily Zhang
Head of Platform, DeeplyHealth
emily.zhang@deeplyhealth.com
+1 415-555-0126
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@deeplyhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DeeplyHealth: tenant access corridor & API key plan

Thanks Emily — great summary. I sketched a lightweight handoff we can execute this week; Ben and Monica are on the plan below.

Plan (high level)
- Day 0 (today): confirm admin roster and SSO metadata. (Owner: DeeplyHealth)
- Day 1: Redwood creates tenant namespaces (staging + prod) and provisions initial admin accounts; seed one service API key into staging for integration tests. (Owner: Ben Carter)
- Day 2: Redwood shares RBW tenant map and staged API key names (we will not paste secrets in email). Provide instructions for connecting Vault -> Redwood KMS integration; Monica to own docs + short call.
- Day 3: DeeplyHealth runs smoke tests, reports any auth failures. If green, Redwood will replicate seeding to prod and lock admin enrollment.

Security artifacts needed from you:
- SOC 2 type II report (or date when available)
- Point-of-contact for security questionnaire (email + preferred hours)

Notes / decisions to validate:
- API keys: we support automated rotation via our control plane for service-account keys; rotation can be scheduled daily/weekly/monthly. We'll recommend weekly for staging and monthly for prod unless you request stricter cadence.
- KMS: we support customer KMS via a TLS endpoint + cert pinning. Monica will send the specific Vault role binding steps.

I attached a short tenant access sketch (rbw tenant map + step checklist). If that plan looks good we can target staging seeded by 2026-12-01 and prod by 2026-12-03. Can do an onboarding call — Monica, Ben, Emily: when are you free?

Attachments: rbw-tenant-map.xlsx, tenant-access-corridor-v1.pdf

Best,
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@deeplyhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DeeplyHealth: tenant access corridor & API key plan

Looping in operational details from my side. I will: 

- Create namespaces: deephealth-staging and deephealth-prod (RBW mapping in rbw-tenant-map.xlsx).
- Create project scaffolds and one seeded service key in staging: name will be dh-staging-service-1 (we'll deliver the secret via the secure console).
- Set IAM roles: Admin (create/delete keys, invite users), Dev (generate tokens for apps), ReadOnly (monitoring). Please confirm the list of people for Admin role in prod.

Quick question for Emily: do you want the initial service key to be long-lived or ephemeral for the smoke tests? We can issue an ephemeral token (24h) to reduce exposure during early-stage testing.

Ben
Senior Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@deeplyhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DeeplyHealth: tenant access corridor & API key plan

Thanks — that timeline works for us. A few quick answers and asks: 

- Admin roster (prod): Mark Rivera, Emily Zhang, Jason Li (infra lead). Staging admins: Mark, Emily.
- For the initial service key please issue an ephemeral 24h token for staging — we will request a longer-lived key only after successful end-to-end tests.
- Attached is our SSO metadata (sso-metadata.xml) and the contact for security questionnaire: jessica.sims@deeplyhealth.com (available M-F 9-5 PT).
- We'd like a 30-minute walkthrough on Dec 2 at 10:00 PT to watch Ben seed staging and validate the smoke test run. Can you send a calendar invite?

Attachments: sso-metadata.xml
